RESUMEN: 6 repos clonados para autopsia (2026-05-25)

1. nanobot (HKUDS, 43K⭐) - Ultra-liviano, Python. Core agente mínimo y legible.
   Estructura: agent/, api/, bus/, channels/, cli/, providers/, security/, skills/, cron/
   Similar a Nexus en filosofia pero con core mucho mas chico.

2. OpenHarness/ohmo (HKUDS, 12.9K⭐) - Harness engineering completo.
   Estructura: src/openharness/ con 43 tools, subagentes, skills loading (.md), MCP, plan mode, schedule/cron.
   Competidor directo de nuestro pipeline de harness. Pub: Abril 2026.

3. OpenFang (RightNow-AI, 17.6K⭐) - Agent OS en Rust. 13 crates.
   Arquitectura: kernel, runtime, hands (autonomous agents), channels (40+), memory (SQLite+vector), skills, api, desktop (Tauri).
   Unique: 7 "Hands" autonomos (Browser, Researcher, Social, Monitor, etc), sandbox WASM, Merkle audit trail.

4. OpenAkita (liuchaoxun, nuevo) - Multi-agente todo-en-uno.
   Estructura: apps/, channels/, plugins/, skills/, tools/, mcps/, auth_api/, identity/
   89 tools, 30+ LLM providers, 6 IM platforms, skill marketplace, auto-evolucion diaria, 8 personas.

5. Pincer (pincerhq, nuevo) - Agente seguro y auditable.
   Codigo Python limpio (~500 files, 4.8MB). Sandbox por subprocess, AST scan skills, hard daily spending cap.
   8 canales (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, Email, Voice), MCP, memoria cross-channel FTS5.

6. Lethe (atemerev, 74⭐) - Asistente autonomo con cognicion de fondo.
   Arquitectura Actor: Cortex (user-facing), Brainstem (supervision health), DMN (background cognition hourly), Hippocampus (recall+salience).
   Memoria: notes/ (persistent knowledge) + LanceDB (archival). Telegram-only. Background cognition unico.

# ANALISIS EXHAUSTIVO: 6 Repos Clonados

## 1. nanobot (HKUDS, 43K⭐) — Ultra-Lightweight Agent
### Datos
- Files: 554, Dirs: 91, Size: 37.5MB
- Lenguaje: Python 3.11+, Licencia: MIT
- Tags: ai-agent, mcp, memory, chat, claude-code, openclaw
- Release: v0.2.0 (2026-05-16), 16 releases
- Homepage: nanobot.wiki

### Arquitectura
- Core: nanobot.py (facade) -> AgentLoop (state machine) -> AgentRunner (tool loop)
- Provider: LLMProvider ABC (base.py) con 14 implementaciones
  anthropic, openai, azure, bedrock, github_copilot, openai_codex, openai_compat, fallback
- AgentLoop state machine: RESTORE->COMPACT->COMMAND->BUILD->RUN->SAVE->RESPOND->DONE
  Con tabla de transiciones event-driven y trace logging
- AgentRunner: loop principal de tool-calling
  1. Context governance (snip, microcompact, budget)
  2. Model request con streaming + retry
  3. Tool execution (paralelo si concurrent_tools=True)
  4. Injection draining (mid-turn messages)
  5. Empty response recovery, length recovery
  6. Error handling con SSRF + workspace violation classification
- ToolRegistry: loader plugin-based, MCP servers, file state tracking
- Memory: Consolidator (token-based), Dream (two-stage), AutoCompact
- Security: network.py (SSRF), workspace isolation, tool-level
- Hooks: AgentHook lifecycle (before_iteration, after_iteration, on_stream, etc.)

### Lo relevante para Nexus
- Provider trait hecho y derecho: LLMProvider ABC con chat() abstractmethod
  + chat_stream, chat_with_retry, fallback provider
- Agente runner reutilizable: AgentRunner es independiente del product-layer
- State machine event-driven: patron a copiar para el Director
- Sistema de tools plugable: ToolRegistry + ToolLoader
- Fallback provider: el que define cadena de modelos alternativos

Rust Programming Language
Performance
Rust is blazingly fast and memory-efficient: with no runtime or
garbage collector, it can power performance-critical services, run on
embedded devices, and easily integrate with other languages.
Reliability
Rust’s rich type system and ownership model guarantee memory-safety
and thread-safety — enabling you to eliminate many classes of
bugs at compile-time.
Productivity
Rust has great documentation, a friendly compiler with useful error
messages, and top-notch tooling — an integrated package manager
and build tool, smart multi-editor support with auto-completion and
type inspections, an auto-formatter, and more.
In 2018, the Rust community decided to improve the programming experience
for a few distinct domains (see
the 2018
roadmap
). For these, you can find many high-quality crates and some
awesome guides on how to get started.
Command Line
Whip up a CLI tool quickly with Rust’s robust ecosystem.
Rust helps you maintain your app with confidence and distribute it with ease.
Building Tools
WebAssembly
Use Rust to supercharge your JavaScript, one module at a time.
Publish to npm, bundle with webpack, and you’re off to the races.
Writing Web Apps
Networking
Predictable performance. Tiny resource footprint. Rock-solid reliability.
Rust is great for network services.
Working On Servers
Embedded
Targeting low-resource devices?
Need low-level control without giving up high-level conveniences?
Rust has you covered.
Starting With Embedded
Hundreds of companies around the world are using Rust in production
today for fast, low-resource, cross-platform solutions.
From startups to large
corporations, from embedded devices to scalable web services, Rust is a great fit.
